$comment: Editorial judgement, deliberately kept in one reviewable file and never mixed with sourced data. Wikidata records awards for only about forty comic volumes, and misses Year One, The Dark Knight Returns, Hush and The Killing Joke entirely, so a curated list is the honest way to cover a measured gap rather than a shortcut around research. Entries resolve against the local catalog by volume name, start year and issue range; anything that does not resolve is reported and skipped rather than guessed at. Tier 1 is a story the hobby treats as canonical, tier 2 is strongly acclaimed, tier 3 is notable.

stories.name: Batman: Year One
stories.note: Miller and Mazzucchelli's origin retelling; the most commonly recommended Batman starting point.

stories.name: Batman: The Long Halloween
stories.note: Loeb and Sale. Eisner Award for Best Limited Series, 1998.

stories.name: Batman: Hush
stories.note: Loeb and Jim Lee; a standard modern entry point and a tour of the supporting cast.

stories.name: Batman: A Death in the Family
stories.note: The death of Jason Todd; a landmark the rest of the character's continuity refers back to.

stories.name: Batman: The Dark Knight Returns
stories.note: Miller. Repeatedly named among the most important superhero comics published.

stories.name: Batman: Dark Victory
stories.note: Direct sequel to The Long Halloween by the same team.

stories.name: Batman: The Killing Joke
stories.note: Moore and Bolland. Defining Joker story, though its treatment of Barbara Gordon is much criticised.

stories.name: Batman: Knightfall
stories.note: Bane breaks Batman; widely known, though long and heavily crossed over.

stories.name: Gotham Central
stories.note: Brubaker, Rucka and Lark. Eisner Award for Best Serialized Story.

stories.name: The New Teen Titans
stories.note: Wolfman and Perez. The definitive run for the Titans and for Dick Grayson and Starfire as a couple.

stories.name: The Judas Contract
stories.note: The high point of the Wolfman and Perez run; Dick Grayson becomes Nightwing.

stories.name: Titans (2016)
stories.note: Abnett's Rebirth run; the modern take on the same cast and relationships.

stories.name: Nightwing: Year One
stories.note: Dixon and Beatty; the standard origin for Dick Grayson as Nightwing.

stories.name: Watchmen
stories.note: Moore and Gibbons. Eisner Award winner and the most widely read work in the medium.

stories.name: Kingdom Come
stories.note: Waid and Ross. Eisner Award for Best Limited Series.

stories.name: All-Star Superman
stories.note: Morrison and Quitely. The most commonly recommended Superman book for a new reader.

stories.name: Superman: Red Son
stories.note: Millar. Self-contained elseworld, frequently recommended as a way in.

stories.name: Superman for All Seasons
stories.note: Loeb and Sale; a quiet, self-contained origin.

stories.name: Superman: Birthright
stories.note: Waid's modern origin retelling.

stories.name: The Death of Superman
stories.note: The most widely reported comic story of its era.

stories.name: Superman/Batman: Public Enemies
stories.note: Loeb and McGuinness; the pair as a double act, adapted to animation.

stories.name: Batman/Superman: World's Finest
stories.note: Waid and Mora; the current, and unusually accessible, take on the partnership.

stories.name: Daredevil: Born Again
stories.note: Miller and Mazzucchelli; routinely named the best Daredevil story.

stories.name: Daredevil: The Man Without Fear
stories.note: Miller and Romita Jr; the standard retold origin.

stories.name: Daredevil (2011)
stories.note: Waid and Samnee. Eisner-winning run and the most approachable modern Daredevil.

stories.name: The Night Gwen Stacy Died
stories.note: The story usually cited as ending the Silver Age of superhero comics.

stories.name: Kraven's Last Hunt
stories.note: DeMatteis and Zeck; the most acclaimed Spider-Man story of the 1980s.

stories.name: Ultimate Spider-Man
stories.note: Bendis and Bagley; written specifically as a way in for new readers.

stories.name: The New Frontier
stories.note: Cooke. Eisner Award for Best Limited Series.

stories.name: Batman: Year 100
stories.note: Pope. Eisner Award for Best Limited Series, though far less read than its reputation suggests.
